description.p: Calculator is a native desktop calculator with Standard, Scientific and Programmer modes over a shared portable calculation core.
The Linux desktop application uses GTK4 and integrates with the system application menu, icon theme and Software Manager through AppStream.
Add a first-class persistent Linux unit converter and pin replacement validation to the exact Linux Mint 22.3 GNOME Calculator 41.1 baseline.
Fix Linux Advanced Tools window ownership so closing the Tools workbench leaves the main Calculator running, while carrying the latest mature expression and unit parity improvements.
Harden Scientific clear-state semantics, canonical exact rational output, extreme-value MPFR validation and interactive latency regression protection.

Complete the advanced calculator roadmap with engineering, conversion, network, storage, date/time, constants, statistics, graphing, equation solving, exact decimal, arbitrary-precision and complex tools across Linux, Windows and iPhone.
Harden engineering notation at binary64 boundaries and expand independent high-precision numerical validation.
Add shared Additional Results with decimal, scientific and engineering representations across Linux, Windows and iPhone.
Complete the Common 1.19.10 semantic appearance integration, add direct Windows result copying, stronger focus/accessibility treatment, and high-precision MPFR numerical validation.
Add simultaneous Programmer BIN/OCT/DEC/HEX representations and selectable result/copy surfaces.
Add structured, recallable calculation history across Linux, Windows and iPhone, including exact Programmer-mode context.
Expand Scientific and Programmer capability with stateful 2nd/HYP/angle/notation controls, rotate and NAND/NOR operators, and explicit memory store while preserving cross-platform parity.
Rebuild Calculator against immutable Common 1.19.8 while preserving the established public ownership boundary and all calculator behaviour.
Deepen Common 1.19.7 reuse, centralise scientific/unary semantics and history rendering, and tighten platform/domain ownership boundaries.
Restore the intended compact Standard-mode geometry with a shared 480-unit desktop contract while retaining taller Scientific and Programmer layouts.
Remove unused vertical space below the Linux Standard keypad while retaining the shared desktop geometry contract.
Bound Programmer parser recursion so excessively nested input fails deterministically instead of risking stack exhaustion.
Unify calculator interaction across Linux, Windows and iPhone, harden parser boundaries, repair desktop geometry and DPI handling, and add native Windows/iPhone artwork.
Enforce the three canonical MB Corpo text faces across Linux, Windows and iPhone while keeping Standard mode compact.
Add AppStream metadata so Linux software centres can associate the Calculator package with its desktop application and icon.
